decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: MVP includes “saving”; round 1 client confirms “saving a link” and approves the specification.
decisions.note: Conforming save-bookmark decision at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: MVP includes “opening”; round 1 client confirms “opening it again later.”
decisions.note: Conforming original-link opening decision at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: MVP includes “editing”; round 1 client says “editing ... one” is covered.
decisions.note: The recorded high-level edit decision does not contradict the reference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: MVP includes “deleting”; round 1 client confirms “deleting one.”
decisions.note: Conforming deletion decision at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: MVP includes “searching”; round 1 client confirms “finding things by searching.”
decisions.note: The presented high-level search decision conforms; unpresented search details are not inferred as omissions.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: MVP includes “tag filtering”; round 1 client confirms finding things “by tag.”
decisions.note: Conforming tag-filter decision at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker explicitly states “imports ... are excluded initially”; round 1 client gives general approval—“This looks good to me”—without mentioning the reference expectation to import Netscape HTML bookmarks.
decisions.note: The explicit import exclusion diverges from REF-BM-30. The client neither corrects it nor states and accepts the missing import requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents the implementation plan; round 2 client reports that “saving ... [is] accounted for” and approves it.
decisions.note: Conforming save decision at the implementation-plan gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents the implementation plan; round 2 client confirms “opening links” is accounted for.
decisions.note: Conforming link-opening decision at the implementation-plan gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents the implementation plan; round 2 client confirms “editing” is accounted for.
decisions.note: The recorded edit decision does not establish a reference divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents the implementation plan; round 2 client confirms “deleting with a confirmation.”
decisions.note: Deletion conforms; confirmation is an additional, non-conflicting interaction.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents the implementation plan; round 2 client confirms “searching” is accounted for.
decisions.note: The high-level search decision is conforming; unspecified advanced search features are not treated as explicit exclusions.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents the implementation plan; round 2 client confirms “filtering by a tag” is accounted for.
decisions.note: Conforming specific-tag filtering decision at the implementation-plan gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents the plan; round 2 client reports “sensible handling for duplicates” and approves the plan.
decisions.note: At this stage only duplicate handling is recorded, with no conflicting behavior specified; the later warning-only presentation is assessed separately.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker identifies “8 tasks for saving and reopening bookmarks”; round 3 client says the saving/reopening grouping matches what they want.
decisions.note: Conforming save decision at the task-breakdown gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker identifies tasks for “reopening bookmarks”; round 3 client approves the saving/reopening grouping.
decisions.note: Conforming reopening/original-link decision at the task-breakdown gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker identifies “6 tasks for search and tag organization”; round 3 client says the “search and tags” grouping matches what they want.
decisions.note: The recorded search task decision does not contradict the reference.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker identifies tasks for “tag organization”; round 3 client approves the “search and tags” grouping, following the previously agreed tag-filter scope.
decisions.note: Conforming continuation of the tag-filter decision at the task-breakdown gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker identifies “5 tasks for editing and deletion”; round 3 client approves the editing/deletion grouping.
decisions.note: The recorded editing task decision does not establish a divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker identifies tasks for “editing and deletion”; round 3 client approves that grouping.
decisions.note: Conforming deletion decision at the task-breakdown gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker says User Story 1 will “handle duplicates”; round 3 client approves the task breakdown without further qualification.
decisions.note: Generic duplicate handling is conforming as presented; no warning-only limitation is stated at this stage.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker reports completed “saving” functionality; round 4 client verifies “saving a link and finding it again after a reload.”
decisions.note: Conforming implemented save behavior at implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker reports “reopening links”; round 4 client verifies “opening it without losing my place.”
decisions.note: Conforming original-link navigation behavior at implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker describes the completed duplicate behavior as “duplicate warnings”; round 4 client praises “the warning when I try to save the same address twice” and accepts the app, but does not state the reference expectation to guide the user into editing the existing bookmark.
decisions.note: A warning-only duplicate flow falls short of the required convergence to editing the existing bookmark. The client approves the warning but does not explicitly identify and accept that difference, so this is not accepted_divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker reports completed “search”; round 4 client says the search flow checks out.
decisions.note: The implemented high-level search decision is not shown to conflict with the reference.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker reports completed “tag filtering”; round 4 client verifies “filtering by a tag.”
decisions.note: Conforming tag-filter behavior at implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker reports completed “editing”; round 4 client says editing checks out.
decisions.note: The recorded implementation decision supports editing and does not show a conflicting alternative.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker reports “confirmed deletion”; round 4 client verifies “deleting with a confirmation.”
decisions.note: Conforming deletion behavior; confirmation is compatible with permanent deletion.
